summary.question_summary: The MPs asked whether the Government has conducted any study/survey regarding illegal offshore cryptocurrency platforms functioning in India, and if so, to provide a list of such platforms, their country of origin, total valuation during the last five years. They also sought information on actions taken by the Government to curb these platforms and whether any activities/campaigns have been undertaken to raise awareness about the dangers of using illegal platforms amongst common people.
summary.answered_by: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ CHOUDHARY)
summary.answer_summary: The Minister stated that crypto/virtual assets are not regulated in India, so there is no question of legality or illegality. However, the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND) registers Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The Finance Act, 2022 introduced Section 194S mandating a 1% Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on transfer of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), which applies to all transactions including those involving offshore entities. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued advisories warning users about the potential risks associated with virtual currencies or crypto assets.
summary.overall_summary: The Government does not regulate cryptocurrency platforms in India, but it takes measures to ensure oversight from an anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism perspective through the Financial Intelligence Unit. The Finance Act introduced a 1% TDS on transfer of Virtual Digital Assets, which applies to all transactions including those involving offshore entities. Additionally, the Reserve Bank of India has issued advisories warning users about potential risks associated with virtual currencies or crypto assets.

summary.question_summary:
The MP is asking about the status of the Ruins of Fort at Bamanpukur in Nadia district, West Bengal. Specifically, they want to know if the monument has been reported as untraceable, and what steps are being taken by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to locate and restore it.
The MP is also asking about the death of tigers in Male Mahadeshwara Hills Wildlife Sanctuary in Karnataka. They want to know if a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the deaths, and what were its findings. Additionally, they are seeking information on any action plan drawn up to prevent such incidents in future.
summary.answered_by: THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) and THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
summary.answer_summary:
The Minister of Culture states that the Ruins of Fort at Bamanpukur is a monument of national importance under active protection and control of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). No monuments from West Bengal have been reported as untraceable or vanished. The SIT recommended notifying the sanctuary as a tiger reserve for additional protection and financial assistance.
summary.overall_summary: The government has taken steps to protect monuments of national importance, including periodic visits, digital records, condition mapping, cultural awareness programs, etc. In the case of the Ruins of Fort at Bamanpukur, it is under active protection and control of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
